title: The image scan of a renamed file judges every finding as new
body:
`-baseline-ref` compares each compose file's findings with the same path on the base branch. A change that renames a
file carrying image pins has no baseline there, so its images' existing findings gate as new. Seen on a catena-templates
blueprint rename (`nextcloud-s3-oidc` to `nextcloud`, catena-templates PR #236): "baseline-ref: no baseline for
blueprints/nextcloud/docker-compose.yml", and the change needed an admin bypass. Callers: catena-templates
`.github/workflows/app-ci.yml:433-442` and the pull request scan of `security.yml`.

- **Behaviour:** a change that renames or moves a file carrying image pins is judged against the file it was renamed
  from (git's rename detection between the base and the head), so only findings the change adds gate.
- **Security notes:** none new; the gate still fails on a finding the change adds, and a file with no rename source is
  judged as new.
- **Acceptance:** a scanctl unit test with a renamed compose file whose findings exist at the old path passes, and one
  that adds a finding while renaming fails; the next rename of a catena-templates app passes its scan with no bypass.

Moved from catenahq/ops#78.

title: Image alerts: a failed image scan freezes the whole images/ category, and a rejected upload stays green
body:
scanctl uploads third-party image findings as tool `trivy-image`, category `images/`, each written run cut to its 5,000
most severe results. Open:

- One image scan failing after its retry leaves the whole `images/` category out of the upload, freezing every image
  alert on that run (catena-templates scans hundreds of images).
- The reusable workflow uploads with `continue-on-error: true` (`.github/workflows/github-reusable.yml:186`), so a
  rejected upload leaves the job green.
- A repository that drops every third-party image keeps its `trivy-image` alerts until that configuration is deleted.

Repository admin steps, no code: delete trivy's old `images` configuration on catena-ce and catena-templates (Security,
Code scanning, Tool status, Trivy, `images`, Delete configuration) once each repository's first scheduled run on the new
scanctl has uploaded `trivy-image`.

An idea for later, not now: a category per image (`images/<image>`), so a failed scan freezes only its image, a push
uploads the images it scanned, and almost nothing is cut (catena-templates: 55 images with findings, median 176, one over
5,000); it needs uploads of at most 20 runs per file and an empty run for each image no longer pinned.

- **Behaviour:** an image alert stays open until a scan of that image no longer finds it; a rejected upload is seen.
- **Security notes:** none; the gate does not read code scanning.
- **Acceptance:** the old configurations deleted; a catena-ce pull request's trivy check reports success; a
  catena-templates scheduled upload is processed; a scheduled run with one failed image scan keeps the other images'
  alerts current.

### Files Scope

- EDIT: `cmd/scanctl/main.go`
- EDIT: `cmd/scanctl/accept.go`
- EDIT: `internal/runner/image.go`
- EDIT: `internal/runner/runner.go`
- EDIT: `internal/report/report.go`
- EDIT: `internal/sarif/sarif.go`
- EDIT: `internal/runner/image_test.go`
- EDIT: `internal/report/report_test.go`
- EDIT: `internal/sarif/sarif_test.go`
- EDIT: `cmd/scanctl/accept_test.go`
- EDIT: `README.md`

`.github/workflows/github-reusable.yml` is not editable from this worker (the token has no workflow scope); its exact
diff is carried in the pull request body for the owner to apply with the merge.

title: A failed scan closes the alerts of a tool and category other scans share
body:
scanctl leaves a category out of its upload only when an image scan in it failed (`internal/runner/image.go`). A failed
trivy file scan on a run whose own images scanned writes trivy's default run with the own-image findings alone, which
closes the file-scan alerts; a failed guarddog scan of one manifest does the same to that manifest's alerts.

- **Behaviour:** an alert stays open until a scan that covers it no longer finds it.
- **Security notes:** none; the gate does not read code scanning.
- **Acceptance:** a unit test on the written report.

### Files Scope

- `README.md`
- `cmd/scanctl/main.go`
- `internal/runner/guarddog.go`
- `internal/runner/image.go`
- `internal/runner/image_test.go`
- `internal/runner/license.go`
- `internal/runner/runner.go`

title: Two tags of one image pinned at once share a code-scanning rule
body:
Image rule ids name the image without its tag (`internal/runner/image.go` `tagImage`), so a CVE reported by two tags of
one image shows the first scan's score on both alerts.

- **Behaviour:** decide whether this case occurs in any repository; if it does, each tag's alert shows its own score.
- **Security notes:** none.
- **Acceptance:** a unit test on the written report with two tags of one image.

Moved from catenahq/ops#238.

title: An expired image acceptance leaves its code-scanning alert dismissed
body:
`--dismiss-baseline` closes the alert of an accepted finding as "won't fix"; when the acceptance expires the finding gates
again, but GitHub keeps the alert dismissed, so the Security tab of catena-ce and catena-templates under-reports what the
scheduled run fails on. The first acceptances expire on 2026-11-18 (catena-ce, catena-admin) and 2027-01-17
(catena-templates).

- **Behaviour:** an alert dismissed by scanctl reopens when its acceptance expires.
- **Security notes:** none; the gate does not read code scanning.
- **Acceptance:** a unit test on `internal/dismiss` with an expired entry (PATCH state=open).

Moved from catenahq/ops#324.

title: setup-go's cache in the scanctl workflow
body:
The reusable workflow saves Go's module and build caches whenever the caller's go.sum or the stable Go changes, pull
request scopes included: 72-89 s on a self-hosted runner's 1.3 MB/s upload. A hit saves about 11 s of scanctl's install
and part of govulncheck's build. Its contents are not checked before `go install` uses them.

- **Behaviour:** the workflow keeps the cache only where it saves more than it costs, by measured step times.
- **Security notes:** none new; removing it removes an unchecked input of the scanner.
- **Acceptance:** step times of three caller runs before and after.

Moved from catenahq/ops#365.

title: Check every scanner file against its pinned digest
body:
scanctl uses scanner files it never checks against a digest.

- **Behaviour:** every scanner file is checked against the digest `tools.lock` pins before use; each fetch and scan
  prints its duration.
- **Security notes:** removes an unchecked input of the scanner.
- **Acceptance:** scanctl unit tests for a changed or digest-less scanner file.

Part of catenahq/ops#362 (The security scan reuses catena-admin's dependency build), which tracks the change across repositories. Blocked by catenahq/catena-admin#239, the part before it in push order.

title: Image alerts: delete the code-scanning category of an image that stops being pinned
body:
## Context

scanctl now gives each third-party image its own code-scanning category, `images/<repository>/`. A run writes a category only for the images it scanned, so an alert opens or closes only on a scan of that image: a failed image scan leaves its own category out and the other images' alerts stay current.

The gap: an image that stops being pinned keeps its code-scanning configuration, and its alerts, until someone deletes it by hand (Security and quality, Code scanning, Tool status, `trivy-image`, the image's category, Delete configuration). README documents that. The images a repo pins are in `scanctl.yml`, so scanctl knows which categories are stale.

## Acceptance

- A run given a new opt-in flag (the shape `--dismiss-baseline` has) deletes the code-scanning analyses of a `trivy-image` category no current `images:` or `image_pins:` entry names, so the stale alerts and their configuration go.
- A category named by a current pin is never touched, including one whose scan failed this run.
- Without the flag nothing is deleted.
- The run says how many categories it removed and names them.
- A repo without `security-events: write`, or a pull request run, skips the deletion with a warning rather than failing (a feature-branch run is not the source of truth for what the org accepted).
- A poll's failure is unknown, never empty: an API error must not read as "no analyses".
- Unit tests stub the GitHub API; no test calls it.

## Reference pattern

`internal/dismiss` already closes a matching alert through the API from `GITHUB_TOKEN`/`GITHUB_REPOSITORY` (`dismiss.FromEnv`, `Client.Dismiss`), skipped on `pull_request`. The deletion wants the same shape: list `GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/analyses?tool_name=trivy-image&per_page=100`, group by `category`, `DELETE /repos/{owner}/{repo}/code-scanning/analyses/{id}?confirm_delete=true`.

## Files Scope

EDIT:
- `cmd/scanctl/main.go`
- `internal/dismiss/dismiss.go`
- `README.md`

NEW: none. A new file under `internal/dismiss/` is fine if the API client grows past one file.

## Verification

- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...`, `go test -count=1 ./...`
- A test that a stale category is deleted, a pinned one is kept, a failed scan's category is kept, and an API error is reported.

Ends the "manual deletion" paragraph in README's code-scanning section.
